name: From dwelling comes desire; from desire, anger
meaning: Dwelling on something breeds attachment, then desire, then anger when it is blocked, then confusion and the loss of judgement.
applies_when: Anger, obsession, cravings or rumination are escalating, and the person wants to see where it starts.
misleads_when: It is used to shame normal wishes or to tell someone their justified anger at injustice is merely a defect.
modern_application: Next time anger rises, trace it back one step: what were you dwelling on just before? Interrupt the chain there.

name: Draw the senses in like a tortoise
meaning: Steady wisdom comes when one can withdraw the senses from their objects at will, as a tortoise draws in its limbs.
applies_when: Constant stimulation (phones, cravings, distractions) is scattering attention.
misleads_when: It becomes rigid suppression or avoidance of ordinary life and pleasures.
modern_application: Create one daily 'tortoise hour': no screens, no snacks, no background noise. Notice what pulls at you.

name: Forcing yourself rarely works; nature prevails
meaning: Beings follow their nature, so mere suppression achieves little; holding back outwardly while dwelling on desire inwardly is self-deception.
applies_when: Someone is trying to change a habit by willpower alone and keeps failing, or is pretending to have given something up.
misleads_when: It is used as an excuse to indulge any impulse ('it's my nature').
modern_application: Instead of fighting the urge head-on, change the setting that triggers it, and replace it with something you value more.

name: Unchecked desire is the inner enemy
meaning: Desire and anger, born of restlessness, cover wisdom as smoke covers fire; they sit in the senses, mind and intellect, and must be mastered.
applies_when: Someone keeps acting against their own values 'as if forced'.
misleads_when: It produces shame about all desire, including healthy love, ambition or pleasure.
modern_application: Name the desire that most often overrides your judgement, and decide in advance what you will do the next time it arises.

name: Desire in harmony with dharma is sacred
meaning: Not all desire is to be fought: desire that does not go against dharma is itself divine.
applies_when: Someone feels guilty for wanting love, family, success or comfort that harms no one.
misleads_when: It is stretched to justify desires that do harm others or betray commitments.
modern_application: Test a desire: does it harm anyone, break a promise or cost your integrity? If not, you may pursue it with a clear conscience.

name: The chariot: intellect drives, mind is the reins
meaning: The body is a chariot, the senses its horses, the mind the reins and the intellect the driver; with understanding at the reins, the senses go where you choose.
applies_when: Someone feels pulled around by impulses and wants a practical picture of self-command.
misleads_when: It is used to look down on people who struggle with impulse control for reasons beyond their choice.
modern_application: When an impulse pulls, ask: who is driving right now, my horses or me? Decide where the chariot is going before you loosen the reins.

name: Be your own friend
meaning: Lift yourself up by your own effort; the self can be one's friend or enemy, depending on whether one has learned to guide oneself.
applies_when: Someone is waiting for rescue and needs to reclaim some agency, gently.
misleads_when: It is used to blame someone who is depressed, grieving or overwhelmed for 'not lifting themselves'. For anyone in distress, present it only as kindness to oneself, alongside real support.
modern_application: Speak to yourself as you would to a friend in the same situation; write down what you would tell them, and take one step of that advice yourself.

name: The restless mind can be held
meaning: Arjuna says the mind is as hard to hold as the wind; Krishna agrees, but says practice and detachment can hold it.
applies_when: Someone despairs of ever calming their mind or overthinking.
misleads_when: It replaces professional help for anxiety disorders or other conditions.
modern_application: Acknowledge the difficulty honestly, as Krishna did, then choose one five-minute practice and repeat it daily for two weeks.

name: Notice which quality is driving you
meaning: Clarity (sattva), restless craving (rajas) and inertia (tamas) take turns dominating the mind; seeing which one is active is the first step out of it.
applies_when: Someone wants to understand their own swings between energy, restlessness and lethargy.
misleads_when: It is used to label people permanently ('he is tamasic') rather than describe passing states.
modern_application: Three times a day, note in one word whether you feel clear, driven or dull. After a week, look for what tends to precede each.

name: Choose the good over the merely pleasant
meaning: The good and the pleasant both present themselves; the wise tell them apart and choose the good, while the careless choose comfort.
applies_when: A choice between short-term comfort and long-term wellbeing: study or scrolling, saving or spending, honesty or ease.
misleads_when: It makes someone distrust every enjoyable thing, or choose hardship for its own sake.
modern_application: For a choice in front of you, ask: how will each option feel at the start, and how will it feel in a year?

name: Pleasures of contact have an end
meaning: Pleasures born of sense contact begin and end, and wear out the senses; the wise do not stake their happiness on them.
applies_when: Someone is chasing a high (shopping, substances, novelty) and finds the satisfaction keeps fading.
misleads_when: It turns into contempt for ordinary joys like food, music or affection.
modern_application: Track one habitual pleasure for a week: how long did the good feeling last each time?

name: Contentment is found within
meaning: The person who is content in the self, whose joy and light are within, is at peace and does not depend on outer things.
applies_when: Someone's happiness depends entirely on external outcomes, possessions or approval.
misleads_when: It is used to tell someone to accept unjust material conditions they could change.
modern_application: Spend ten minutes doing nothing but noticing what is already well right now.

name: No one is satisfied by wealth
meaning: Desire is as hard to satisfy as fire; Nachiketas observes that no one is ever satisfied by wealth.
applies_when: Someone is sacrificing health, relationships or integrity for ever more money or status.
misleads_when: It is used to dismiss real poverty or the legitimate need for financial security.
modern_application: Write down the amount that would be 'enough' and what you would do differently once you have it. Ask whether you could start some of it now.

name: Desire, anger and greed: the three gates of harm
meaning: Desire, anger and greed are the threefold gate to self-destruction; freed from them, a person does what is truly good for themselves.
applies_when: Someone is about to act out of rage, lust or greed and wants a quick check.
misleads_when: It is used to condemn a person rather than an action or a state.
modern_application: Before a big decision, ask which of the three, if any, is speaking. If one is, sleep on it.

name: Withstand the surge of desire and anger
meaning: Whoever can withstand the force of desire and anger here, in this life, is disciplined and happy.
applies_when: Someone is in the grip of a strong urge or a flash of anger right now.
misleads_when: It encourages bottling up feelings instead of expressing them safely.
modern_application: When the surge comes, do not act for ten breaths. Urges peak and fall like waves.

name: A resolute mind is single-pointed
meaning: The resolute mind has one direction; the irresolute mind branches endlessly, especially when chasing pleasure and power.
applies_when: Someone is scattered across too many goals and finishing none.
misleads_when: It becomes tunnel vision that ignores other responsibilities or warning signs.
modern_application: Choose one goal for the next 30 days. Write the others on a 'later' list so they stop pulling at you.

name: Calm comes before clear understanding
meaning: In a calm mind sorrows end and understanding soon becomes steady; without calm there is no peace, and without peace no happiness.
applies_when: Someone is trying to make a decision while agitated.
misleads_when: It delays urgent action that cannot wait, such as getting to safety.
modern_application: Before deciding, calm the body first: slow breathing for two minutes, then write the decision in one sentence.

name: Draw the mind inward, step by step
meaning: Meditation moves inward in stages: speech into mind, mind into intellect, intellect into the peaceful Self, until the senses and mind rest.
applies_when: Someone wants a concrete method of meditation for calm and insight.
misleads_when: It is offered as a substitute for medical care, or practised in a way that increases distress (some people with trauma need guided support).
modern_application: Sit for five minutes: first go quiet in speech, then notice thoughts without following them, then rest in simple awareness.

name: The senses face outward; the wise turn within
meaning: We are built to look outward; only rarely does someone, seeking what lasts, turn their gaze inward and find the Self.
applies_when: Someone has achieved outward goals and still feels empty.
misleads_when: It is used to dismiss outward responsibilities and relationships.
modern_application: For one week, end each day with five minutes of honest reflection: what did I learn about myself today?

name: What you consume shapes your state
meaning: Food and habits are of three kinds and shape the mind: wholesome food supports vitality and cheer, harsh food brings pain, stale food brings dullness.
applies_when: Someone notices that diet, substances or media intake affect their mood and energy.
misleads_when: It turns into food moralising or disordered eating.
modern_application: For a week, note how you feel two hours after each meal, and after each hour of media. Keep what leaves you clearer.

name: Stay vigilant: steadiness comes and goes
meaning: Even the wise can be carried away by the senses, and the state of yoga arises and fades, so one must stay watchful.
applies_when: Someone has made progress (sobriety, a new habit, calm) and is relaxing their guard.
misleads_when: It creates constant fear of relapse instead of steady care.
modern_application: Write down your three biggest triggers and one plan for each, and look at it weekly even when things are going well.
